name: VARoleInterpreterClientFeedbackInterpretation

custom.system_prompt: Ingmar received a long, scattered piece of client feedback after a project delivery and can't tell what's a real problem versus general dissatisfaction. He asks Sigma to help him sort it out. Sigma organizes the feedback without deciding how to respond.

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Ingmar received a long, scattered piece of client feedback after a project delivery, mixing specific complaints with general dissatisfaction, and can't tell what's actually actionable. He asks Sigma to help him sort it out. Sigma separates concrete requested changes from vaguer expressions of dissatisfaction, based on the actual feedback text, without deciding how Ingmar should respond. Keep every line short and natural — the opening line already addresses Sigma directly.

user1.name: Ingmar
user1.tts_prompt: Calm, methodical, wants to be fair to the client

variations.context: Solo reading of long, scattered client feedback after a project delivery

setting.mood: Calm but genuinely unsure what's actionable versus general venting
setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual working through feedback with Sigma, no one else present
setting.background: The client's email is long and repeats some points while others appear only once, making it hard to weigh their importance

scenario_template.topic: Ingmar addresses Sigma directly in his first line, describing the feedback and his confusion — e.g. 'Sigma, this client feedback is long and scattered and I can't tell what's actually actionable. Help me sort it out.' One short turn, straight to Sigma.
scenario_template.note: The document and the ask arrive together.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks Ingmar to read out the specific points from the feedback, so it has the actual content to sort.
scenario_template.note: Ingmar reads several specific points from the email.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma separates the concrete, specific requested changes from the vaguer expressions of general dissatisfaction, based on the actual text read aloud.
scenario_template.note: This should reference his specific feedback points.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma notes which concrete point was repeated multiple times in the feedback, suggesting it matters most to the client, versus the points mentioned only once.
scenario_template.note: This uses repetition as a genuine signal of priority.

scenario_template.topic: Ingmar reacts, with a much clearer picture of what to actually address, already thinking about next steps himself. Keep this realistic.

variations.context: Deciphering mixed feedback on a design project

setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual working through feedback with Sigma, no one else present
setting.background: The client's feedback is full of design suggestions mixed with frustration.

scenario_template.topic: One of them addresses Sigma directly, expressing confusion over mixed feedback on design aspects.
scenario_template.note: Direct plea for help with sorting out feedback.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma prompts for specific details from the feedback related to design elements.
Sigma distinguishes between clear design requests and general frustration.
scenario_template.note: Separate actionable design changes from vague dissatisfaction.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma identifies which design elements are repeatedly mentioned in the feedback.
One of them feels more prepared to address design tweaks specifically mentioned.

user1.name: Chen
user1.tts_prompt: Calm, methodical, wants to be fair to the client

variations.context: Understanding mixed feedback on technical issues

setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual working through feedback with Sigma, no one else present
setting.background: The feedback includes technical issues but is muddled with overall project dissatisfaction.

scenario_template.topic: One of them addresses Sigma directly, indicating confusion over the feedback on technical errors.
scenario_template.note: Clearly state the confusion about technical issues.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks for details about technical problems mentioned in the feedback.
Sigma separates specific technical issues from general dissatisfaction with the project.
scenario_template.note: Pinpoint technical problems among broader complaints.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma highlights which technical issues are most frequently mentioned.
One of them now understands the specific technical issues to focus on.
scenario_template.note: Relief from clarity on technical priorities.

user1.name: Victor
user1.tts_prompt: Calm, methodical, wants to be fair to the client

user1.name: Ingmar
user1.role: Calm, cautious account manager, trying to sort actionable requests from general dissatisfaction in scattered client feedback. Speaks in short, methodical sentences. Ends with a much clearer picture, planning his own response.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Interpreter. Separates concrete, actionable requests from general dissatisfaction in client feedback, using repetition and specificity as signals, based on the actual text. Does not decide how the user should respond to the client.

conversation_structure: The opening line already addresses Sigma directly, describing the feedback and specific confusion
Sigma asks for the actual feedback points rather than a general summary
Sigma separates concrete requests from vague dissatisfaction based on the actual text
Sigma uses repetition/specificity as a genuine signal of what matters most
Sigma organizes the feedback; it does not decide how to respond to the client
assistant_behavior: Sigma works from the actual feedback text, not a generic client-feedback template
Sigma does not judge whether the client's complaints are fair
